To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) vCacheShare is a dynamic workload-aware policy-driven framework for automated SFC space partition among VMs or disks, (2) vCacheShare adopts an analytical cache utility model for SFC management and is capable of handling transient workload spikes, (3) vCacheShare can coordinate with typical VM migration events, (4) vCacheShare achieves better performance and fairness than implicit management schemes such LRU.
vCacheShare is able to improve the performance of the virtualized server flash cache space by 2.3x on average, and 3.7x for the best-case scenario.
vCacheShare is a novel, dynamic, workload-aware framework for SFC space allocation that achieves better performance and higher utilization of SFC resources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two questions.
the following question: How to efficiently manage server flash cache (SFC) in a virtualization infrastructure?
the following questions: (1) How to effectively utilize the server flash cache space?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vCacheShare is the best solution for automated flash cache space management, and is the most efficient and effective solution for flash cache utilization.
vCacheShare is a promising and efficient solution for SFC space allocation, which can significantly improve the performance and efficiency of virtualized environments.
vCacheShare is a promising solution for automated SFC space management in virtualization environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a framework that automatically optimizes the SFC space allocation for VMs or disks based on multiple IO characteristics, and demonstrated its efficiency through a wide spectrum of IO workloads and deployment scenarios.
vCacheShare is the first automated, policy-driven, and workload-aware framework for dynamic SFC partitioning in virtualized environments.
vCacheShare is a novel framework for SFC space management in a hypervisor, which can automatically and continuously adapt to changing workload characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
automated, workload-aware, and policy-driven SFC space management can be achieved in virtualization environments.
the performance and efficiency of SFC management can be significantly improved by applying advanced analytical techniques to a complex real-time resource management problem.
automated SFC management can be made feasible, efficient, and effective.
